proposed_from.topic: Fourier-separated honest inference for partial-order Cholesky effect fibers. Fix dimension p, treatment T, outcome Y, known strict partial order P, confidence level alpha, spectral bounds 0<lambda<Lambda, envelope constants 0<c<C, known finite ray exponents q_u bounded by Q on coordinate and pair-sum rays, and E||X||^8<=M8. Observe iid X=U+G_Gamma, where G_Gamma is independent centered Gaussian, lambda I<=Gamma<=Lambda I is the greatest Gaussian-divisor covariance, and U is generated by finitely many independent nonconstant Gaussian-indecomposable sources with bounded loadings and c(1+|t|)^(-q_u)<=|phi_U(tu)|<=C(1+|t|)^(-q_u) for |t|>=1. Construct explicit measurable finite-sample simultaneous ray and covariance regions using centered empirical characteristic-function moduli, polarization, spectral clipping, and a bounded fallback. Enumerate predecessor ideals and return the union of covariance-region images for the full compatible total-effect fiber Theta_TY(Gamma,P); prove uniform whole-fiber coverage and O(1/log N) excess radius and expected Hausdorff error, including exact effect-collision strata without a swap margin. On the explicit exponent-two three-variable subclass with fixed common envelope constants and sufficiently generous fixed eighth moment containing the smooth Laplace--Student splice, prove matching logarithmic covariance, singleton-effect, and honest-confidence diameter lower bounds along Gamma(s)=Gamma1+s aaT. For literal standardized-Laplace sources with loadings bounded away from zero, prove root-N recovery by fourth cumulants as a parametric boundary. Credit Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi for mixed-noise finite identification, Meister (2006) for scalar fixed-envelope centering and lower pairs, and Belomestny--Trabs--Tsybakov (2019) for multivariate polarization. CRAN pcalg::ida and the Maathuis et al. yeast intervention-ranking workflow are the consumer: under an audited mixed-noise/Fourier model, report an honest compatible-effect set rather than a selected Gaussian-causal-sufficiency list. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Derived simultaneous finite-sample covariance regions, whole-fiber coverage, and O(1/log N) expected Hausdorff error. The lower splice fits an explicit class with p=3, lambda=1/10, Lambda=4, c=2/5, C=60, exponent two, eighth moment at most 50000000, and reduced loading norm at most three; its zero polynomial moments give exact eighth-moment accounting. Embedding a=(1,2/5,1) along Gamma(s)=Gamma1+s aaT keeps the equality-stratum effect equal to (3/5+s)/(1+s), giving the causal lower pair. Checks covered 577 legal orders, divisor status, empirical zeros, collision strata, positive definiteness, and the literal-Laplace cumulant boundary; direct donor comparisons found no same whole-fiber theorem. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently verify the uniform Fourier-derivative and weighted-Plancherel estimates in Lemmas 7--8 for m=6 and the displayed cutoff, including their uniform constants. EARLY KILL TEST: Recheck that the m=6 smooth splice stays positive, satisfies the common envelopes and fixed eighth moment, and has vanishing product-experiment divergence; failure invalidates the matching lower claim. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest population result is Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi's finite mixed-noise SCM identification, and the closest statistical donor is Belomestny--Trabs--Tsybakov's latent Gaussian covariance recovery. The direct causal-inference comparator is Wang--Kolar--Drton: Algorithm 3 and Lemma 1 turn an asymptotically valid confidence set for an identifiable additive-error ordering plus conditional adjustment-set intervals into asymptotic coverage of one total effect. Theorem 2 establishes the strict regime-and-guarantee distinction: the published additive-error class and the present latent mixed-noise class are nonnested, and the explicit characteristic-function event gives finite-sample simultaneous inclusion of every point of the partial-order Cholesky fiber, including coincident branches, without order selection. Strieder--Drton's partial-homoscedasticity regions are also adjacent but rely on structural-error variance equalities in a causally sufficient model. Proposition 2 is supporting algebra rather than the novelty center. The field-tier case rests on the mixed-noise whole-fiber theorem together with the conditional matched logarithmic frontier; the smooth-splice construction remains openly unresolved. Scalar centering, polarization, and fourth-cumulant recovery are donors rather than novelty.

proposed_from.literature_map: Sanjaroonpouri and Ramazi, Theorems 2--3 and Corollary 2, identify a finite Cholesky-indexed equivalence class under Gaussian noise and Gaussian-indecomposable confounders but do not quantify sampling uncertainty. Belomestny, Trabs, and Tsybakov, equations (4)--(5) and Theorems 1, 5, and 6, use characteristic-function log moduli, coordinate and pair-sum polarization, and Fourier-domain testing to estimate a latent Gaussian covariance at logarithmic rates; their target is covariance rather than a causal fiber. Meister, equations (2), (4), and (16)--(18), supplies the scalar fixed-envelope centering and least-favorable variance compensation, while its published lower pair does not satisfy the eighth-moment class used here. Strieder and Drton invert tests for total-effect regions under equal error variances, and Wang, Kolar, and Drton retain causal orderings by residual-bootstrap goodness-of-fit tests; both use different identifying models. Perkovi\'c, Kalisch, and Maathuis adapt IDA to maximal PDAGs with background knowledge and motivate enumeration of all compatible effects. Miettinen, Taskinen, Nordhausen, and Oja derive fourth-moment ICA estimating equations and pointwise asymptotic laws, which supplies the fast parametric boundary but not the shrinking-separation transition. Kato and Sasaki construct uniform deconvolution bands with an auxiliary error sample, a resource absent from the present model. The bounded target--method searches found no paper combining greatest-Gaussian-divisor recovery, predecessor-ideal effect enumeration, simultaneous whole-fiber coverage, collision-stratum lower bounds, and a cumulant boundary.
